Execute the 1880 census search for plan item pli_001. The subject is Sarah Ann Mullen Price — but note that 'Mullen' is her middle given name (her mother's maiden surname), not her own surname. Her surname is Price. Search accordingly.

{
  "id": "pli_001",
  "sequence": 1,
  "record_type": "census",
  "jurisdiction": "Dodge County, Wisconsin",
  "date_range": "1880",
  "repository": "FamilySearch",
  "rationale": "The 1880 census should show Sarah (age ~5) in a household, with the head of household confirming whether her surname is Price (father's family) or Mullen (mother's maiden family). The 1880 census also records relationship to head.",
  "fallback_for": null,
  "status": "in_progress"
}
subject:

  "subjectId": "I1",

    {

      "type": "BirthName"
    }

  },
  "death": null
}

agent_returns.text:
- Search run: log_001 (positive). I searched the surname as Price, with "Sarah Ann Mullen" as the given name, in the 1880 census for Dodge County, Wisconsin, with birth years 1873–1877. The census wiki page confirms the 1880 schedule records relationship to head and the parents' birthplaces.
- Top match: "Sarah M. Price in household of James Price" (record WICN-1880-P01). It is indexed as born about 1875 in Wisconsin and living in Dodge County in 1880. The matchScore is 0.91 and it is not attached to any tree person. The birth-year gap is 0 and the place is consistent, so there is no needs-review flag on those checks. I have not read the record itself, so her indexed relationship to the head (daughter or other) is unconfirmed, and so is the Mullen link through her mother. This is an index entry only.
- Second result: Sarah Price, born about 1870 in New York, in Thomas Price's household in Milwaukee County (score 0.24). The birth year and place do not fit, so I'm not treating her as the subject. I wrote no namesake row, since that ground is weaker than the tool's flags.
- Extraction: none ran. No sources or assertions exist yet for these findings; they sit only in the search log.
- Plan item pli_001 stays in_progress.
- Next step: extract the top record to read the household. The household's mother's maiden name or the head's relationship would test the Mullen connection.

---

I looked in the 1880 U.S. census for Dodge County, Wisconsin, for a young girl named Sarah Price, born about 1875. "Mullen" was treated as her middle name, not her surname. One good candidate turned up: a Sarah M. Price, about five years old, born in Wisconsin and living in the household of a James Price. A second Sarah Price, born in New York and living in a different county, doesn't fit.

Next, the candidate's household record can be read in full to confirm whether James Price is her father and whether the family connects to the Mullen name.
